findings.title: Commit subject violates ticket-prefix format
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; the subject 'epmcdme-14786: add planning artifacts' uses a lowercase ticket prefix and description.
findings.impact: Breaks ticket-prefix tooling and history conventions; documented blocking commit-format standard.
findings.recommendation: Reword the commit to 'EPMCDME-14786: Add planning artifacts' or ensure the squash subject conforms.

finding_status.notes: assistant.py is_shared_with: id guard removed from the top; is_global and project-shared branches run first, `not self.id` now sits with the external-user check before the grant lookup. Two tests added.

delete_assistant opens one session; remove_all_grants(..., session) no longer commits; commit only after assistant.delete() succeeds. Test with a raising delete asserts no commit. assistant.delete() still uses its own session, so a commit failure after it could leave orphan grants (visible and revocable per CR-008).
permission.py named_grant_resource_ids now returns Select | None.
test_ability.py compiles the predicate on the postgresql dialect and asserts the three = comparisons and bound params. Not run.
SharedWithResponse.shared_with and SharableUsersResponse.users typed list[dict[str, str | None]].
q is now Query(..., min_length=2), required; test asserts 422 and no service call when omitted.
Future import added; assistant params annotated; returns parameterized in the share service.
list_shared_with now lists orphan grants (user not found) so the owner can revoke them; test added.
PermissionCreationService.run raises PermissionAccessDenied for ResourceType.ASSISTANT before any ability check or save; new untracked test covers it.
kind evidence. fix_evidence has only a waiver decision (no artifacts, no exit-0 commands), and a decision record cannot resolve an evidence finding. Re-kind as a decision to accept the waiver.
